verdicts.reason: User at CLIENT01 opens RDP. The target rdp01.1sn0s.lab is labelled in the background. No private key has formed yet. The Root CA is not involved.
An amber pending pulse travels the floor channel from the client to the rdp01 rack. Nothing is shown as trusted. No private key has formed yet.
The pulse arrives and the amber listener lights on the server. The server, not the client, is the identity owner. No private key has formed yet.

A pale 'Self-signed' card is presented from the listener. The client shows 'Unverified', the channel stays amber, and in strip tiles 5-6 and frame c the attempt ends: the pulse dies and the channel goes dark. Nothing is accepted. The self-seal is too small to read at this tier, but the card is not shown as unsigned. No CA-key private key is involved.
The RDPAuth badge travels from the 1SN0S.LAB AD node onto the rdp01 chassis (frame b, strip tiles 3-6). No client connection is pending. No private key has formed yet.

A key pair forms inside the opened rdp01 chassis. RDP private key (KEY-RDP-PRIV, the white key with a round padlock-style bow): it forms inside the chassis next to the open key container, partly behind the octagon lock plate in frame c and in tiles 3-6. The plain ring public key is beside it. Both stay inside the server.

RDP private key: it drops from the plate area into the open container in strip tile 2 (padlock-bow key at the container mouth). The lid closes in tiles 3-4. In frame c and tiles 4-6 it is locked inside KC-RDP and the anchor bracket is visible. Only the public ring key remains outside. This beat is correct as drawn.

RDP private key: it is not in its container. The locator puts KEY-RDP-PRIV at [517,129,611,194] in f0593 and [520,106,634,185] in f0627, on top of REQ-RDP ([510,134,631,199] and [509,112,655,193]), while KC-RDP is at [317,293,477,440]. In the image, a small white loop bow is attached to the top-left of the request capsule (frame b about x540 y135, frame c about x550 y110, strip tiles 2-6). The locked container in the lower left is empty of its key. The private key has left its container and travels with the request capsule (F-03, F-04). The caption 'The request is signed, not the key sent' is contradicted on screen.

RDP private key: still attached to the request capsule. The locator gives KEY-RDP-PRIV [521,101,638,183] in f0634, [513,137,604,200] in f0675 and [492,139,584,203] in f0717, overlapping REQ-RDP each time; KC-RDP is at about [265-314,297-306,...]. The bow nub is visible on top of the capsule in frame a (about x550 y105), in frame b and c as ring flanges on the capsule, and in tiles 1-6. The beam from the container seals a capsule that already carries the private key, so the proof-of-possession beat shows key material inside the request (F-03, F-04).

RDP private key: it leaves the chassis with the capsule. In f0765 the locator gives KEY-RDP-PRIV [489,347,544,391] against REQ-RDP [480,347,560,396], with KC-RDP at [199,402,315,514] in the chassis. In f0807 it gives [569,361,602,392] against capsule [560,361,613,397]. The capsule with its nub sits outside the server beside the AD pillar's base (frame b, strip tiles 2-3) and at the chassis' right side (frame c, tiles 4-6). The capsule does not enter AD, but a private key is travelling in a moving object (F-03).

RDP private key: it travels along the lit route into Issuing CA 1 inside the request capsule. The locator gives KEY-RDP-PRIV [581,346,612,374] with REQ-RDP [573,345,623,378] in f0814, [477,299,501,318] with [472,299,508,320] in f0840, and [413,215,448,239] with [410,216,455,241] in f0867, which is inside the CA1 vault. KC-RDP is left behind at the server ([408,386,491,459] in f0814; [839,352,953,436] in f0840). The route goes only to Issuing CA 1 (good for F-05), but the RDP server's private key is delivered to the CA (F-03 BLOCKER).

RDP private key: inside the Issuing CA 1 vault, attached to the capsule during the four checks. The locator gives [434,217,476,247] in f0874, [441,145,512,195] in f0930 and [372,159,441,213] in f0987, each inside the REQ-RDP box. A dark key-tooth nub hangs under the capsule in frame c (about x415 y215). CA1's module key (KEY-CA1-PRIV) stays inside its pale module block. The four checks resolve, but the CA is shown holding the requester's private key (F-03). The 'Requester authenticated' tick is also hidden behind the 1SN0S Issuing CA 1 label.

The RDP request is consumed (REQ-RDP is not listed after f1009). The RDP private key is not consumed and does not go home. It moves to Issuing CA 1's signing press: the locator gives [550,108,602,145] in f1009, [470,159,514,190] in f1035 and [432,176,467,200] in f1077, and the white hook-shaped key is visible under the press head in frame b (about x475 y170), frame c (about x445 y185) and strip tiles 3-6. KC-RDP has no listed position here. CA1's own key is in its module ([251,213,266,224]-type box inside MODULE-CA1). With the RDP server's key at the press, the shot reads as the end-entity's private key taking part in the CA's signing (F-03).

The card and its translucent CA1 copy return to rdp01, but the RDP private key stays in Issuing CA 1. In f1110 the locator gives KEY-RDP-PRIV [354,184,368,194] at depth 23.45 m, beside MODULE-CA1 at 23.49 m, while KC-RDP is at [554,343,625,403] at depth 9.55 m. The white hook is visible at the CA1 press in frame b (about x360 y185) and tiles 1-3. The certificate locks beside an emptied container, not 'beside the existing private key', so the one-identity pairing (F-09) and keys-stay-home (F-03) are both contradicted.

The root presentation is itself correct: a sealed gold vault on a cable-free plinth, a self-seal ring revealed, and the root's module and press dark and still (frames b-c, tiles 3-6). However, the RDP private key is still inside the Issuing CA 1 vault: [318,198,330,207] in f1144, inside the CA1 vault in frame a, while KC-RDP is at [371,317,430,373] in the rdp01 chassis. In f1193 and f1242 it is off-frame below. The root's own key (KEY-ROOT-PRIV) is inside MODULE-ROOT. Because a key sits outside its owner, the beat is WRONG (F-03).

The ceremony content is acceptable. The flashback is desaturated and marked 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony'. The tagged 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' reaches the root plinth (frame b, tiles 2-3) on removable media (white chips on the floor). The root's key stays in MODULE-ROOT ([743,293,765,307] inside [719,270,793,334] in f1320), and CA1's key stays in MODULE-CA1. However, the RDP server's private key appears in this setup-era flashback, inside Issuing CA 1 at the press: [821,167,896,215] in f1246 and [770,169,837,213] in f1249, the white hook beside the press head in T-cut f1246 (about x835 y185) and frame a (about x800 y180), [359,148,391,170] in f1392 (frame c, about x375 y155), and tiles 1, 5 and 6. A key that did not exist at setup is shown sitting in a CA, which implies the end-entity key lives in the CA (F-03).

The issuer link joins CA1's crown certificate to the root, the root stays cable-free and its module is dark, and no end-entity request goes to the root. However, the RDP private key is still inside the CA1 vault: [434,400,442,406] in f1448, inside the CA1 vault in frame b, and [449,361,454,366] in f1458. KC-RDP is off-frame ([609,766,...]). The issuer link is also drawn plain white rather than gold-to-cyan.

A new amber pulse runs to rdp01 and the server card plus CA1 copy travel to the client (frame c, tiles 4-6). However, the RDP private key is in the Issuing CA 1 vault: [723,178,730,183] in f1545, inside the CA1 vault at top centre-right of frame b, and [604,193,609,197] in f1537, near CA1. It is not in the server's container, so the 'key pulse inside the closed key container' cannot represent the server proving possession. No handshake-proof signature impression is visible in any frame or tile. The beat therefore misrepresents F-10 and F-03.

The chain docks upward: server card, then CA1 card, then the gold root already in its cradle, with an 'Installed earlier by policy' shimmer. Nothing travels from AD. However, the RDP private key cannot be located. The locator gives far off-frame positions in f1594 and f1615 ([3506,...] and [21399,...], the CA1 side) and no entry at all for f1639-f1710. Its last on-screen position was the Issuing CA 1 vault, and it was never shown back in KC-RDP. Under the protocol an unlocatable key is WRONG (F-03).

The AIA indicator says 'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it / Fetching never creates trust', nothing is fetched, and the kiosk is passive. This is correct for F-11. However, the RDP private key has no locator entry for f1711-f1770 and is not visible. Its last known place is Issuing CA 1, not its container (F-03).

Ticks 1-5 resolve in order and 'Revocation OK' shows as pending (frame c, tile 6), which is correct for F-12. However, the RDP private key has no locator entry for f1771-f1920 and is not visible. Its last known place is the Issuing CA 1 vault (F-03).

Two amber CRL scrolls come from the pki.1sn0s.lab kiosk, one to each non-root card, and none to the root (frame c, tiles 2-6). 'OCSP if deployed' sits on the client's check list. This is correct for F-13 and AR-07. However, the RDP private key is off-frame right with the Issuing CA 1 vault: [1762,532,...] in f1939, [1553,394,...] in f1965 and [1167,215,...] in f2007, while the rdp01 chassis seen in frame b and tile 3 shows no key in a container. The caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' also appears in frame c while the channel is still amber (F-03).

The channel turns from amber to green only after all six ticks, and the session window opens, which is correct. However, the RDP private key is off-frame right at Issuing CA 1: [1190,209,...] in f2014, [1592,193,...] in f2055 and [1749,181,...] in f2097. It is not in KC-RDP, so the 'trusted' session rests on a server that no longer holds its key (F-03).

The camera glides to WEB01 (portal.1sn0s.lab), whose WebServer-TLS badge is mostly hidden behind the WEB01 label. The web key has not formed yet. However, the rdp01 chassis in frame a and tile 1 is open and shows its key container without the private key. KEY-RDP-PRIV is off-frame at CA1 ([1356,166,...] in f2104), behind the AD pillar inside the CA1 vault in f2145 ([501,169,507,175]), and inside the CA1 vault in f2187 ([280,175,290,182]). This is an emptied container with the key held at the CA (F-03).

Web private key (KEY-WEB-PRIV): it forms in the open WEB01 chassis and drops into KC-WEB (tile 2), and the lid closes. The locator gives [445,243,503,287] inside KC-WEB [414,227,537,320] in f2235 and [453,244,520,295] inside [415,226,561,335] in f2277. The beam seals a clean capsule with no nub (frame c, tiles 4-6). This web flow is correct. However, the RDP private key is still in the Issuing CA 1 vault: [251,169,261,177] in f2194 at the vault edge in frame a, and [147,114,164,127] in f2277 (F-03).

Web key: locked in KC-WEB in all frames (for example [506,288,563,331] inside [478,270,595,367] in f2302, and [704,417,724,429] inside [695,407,735,443] in f2382). The web capsule waits at WEB01 while a steel-blue query diamond runs to AD. Issuing CA 1 is tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here' and CA2 carries the four eligibility tags, which is correct for F-05 and AR-04. However, CA1's vault still reads cyan rather than muted grey. The RDP private key is inside the CA1 vault at the press: [259,173,269,180] in f2382 (frame c, about x265 y175) and [147,114,...] in f2284 (F-03).

Web key: inside KC-WEB ([672,393,691,404] inside [664,384,701,417] in f2389, [453,402,480,421] inside [445,389,491,440] in f2423). The clean web capsule travels only along the violet route into Issuing CA 2, never to CA1 or the root, which is correct. However, the RDP private key remains in the Issuing CA 1 vault: [255,171,266,177]-type box in f2389, inside the CA1 vault top-left of frame a, and off-frame left in f2423 and f2457 (F-03).

Compressed checks run inside Issuing CA 2 with the 'Name supplied in request - enrollment restricted' note, but the note overlaps check 4. CA2's module key stays in its module. The web key is off-frame in KC-WEB at the web server. However, the RDP private key is off-frame left at Issuing CA 1 ([-1417,193,...] in f2464, [-1440,102,...] in f2523, [-847,104,...] in f2562), not in KC-RDP (F-03).

The web capsule is consumed at the CA2 press. The TLS card shows portal.1sn0s.lab and 'Server Authentication' and returns to WEB01 with a CA2 copy. No foreign key appears at CA2's press. Web key: in KC-WEB ([422,276,459,302] inside [410,266,473,322] in f2646, [403,504,478,558] inside [377,473,510,614] in f2697). However, the RDP private key is still off-frame at Issuing CA 1 ([-383,186,...] in f2569, [-189,240,...] in f2697) (F-03).

CA2's existing crown certificate is revealed with a link to the same root. The root's module and press stay dark and the root has no cables, which is correct for F-15 and AR-02. The links are white rather than gold. Web key: in KC-WEB ([186,460,190,468] inside [180,456,197,474] in f2754). However, the RDP private key is inside the Issuing CA 1 vault: [200,353,207,360] in f2745 (CA1 vault at left of frame b) and [412,290,415,295] in f2787 (F-03).

The browser chain portal.1sn0s.lab, then CA2, then the gold root docks at the client, the compressed ticks resolve and the channel turns green (tiles 4-6). No handshake-proof impression and no CRL scroll fetches are visible in any frame or tile. Web key: in KC-WEB ([294,422,297,429] inside [288,419,303,434] in f2794). However, the RDP private key is inside the Issuing CA 1 vault: [870,181,881,188] in f2937 (frame c, inside the CA1 vault at right) and [908,216,915,221] in f2865 (F-03).

Hero topology: the root on top, both issuing CAs below, the RDP server under CA1 and WEB01 under CA2. Cyan and violet paths rise into white links at the single root, and the root stays cable-free and dark. Web key: in KC-WEB ([674,435,680,440] inside [670,431,685,445] in f3117). However, the RDP private key is inside the Issuing CA 1 vault: [389,357,397,362] in f3030 (inside the CA1 vault in frame b) and [424,326,429,330] in f3117 (inside the CA1 vault in frame c), not under it in rdp01 (F-03).

The title card 'Certificate Flow - From request to trust' plays and the shot fades to black. Web key: in KC-WEB ([673,433,679,438] inside [669,429,684,443] in f3124). However, the RDP private key ends the film inside the Issuing CA 1 vault: [425,325,429,329] in f3124 (inside the CA1 vault in frame a) and [446,244,450,247] in f3267. It is never returned to KC-RDP (F-03).

findings.evidence: After locking in KC-RDP in B-03.2, KEY-RDP-PRIV reappears on the request capsule. The locator gives it at [517,129,611,194] with REQ-RDP at [510,134,631,199] in f0593, while KC-RDP is at [317,293,477,440]. A small white padlock-bow loop sits on the top-left of the capsule in frames b and c (about x540 y135 and x550 y110) and in all six strip tiles, and it is still there through B-03.4.
findings.why: The private key is shown leaving its locked container and attached to the request. This contradicts 'Private keys never leave their owner' and 'No private key is ever shown inside a request ... or any moving object', and the on-screen caption 'The request is signed, not the key sent'.
findings.direction: The private key must stay in KC-RDP from B-03.2 to the end. The capsule should carry only the public key and request info, with the seal applied by the beam alone.

findings.evidence: KEY-RDP-PRIV moves with REQ-RDP out of the chassis to the outbound port ([489,347,544,391] in f0765), along the route ([477,299,501,318] in f0840), and into the Issuing CA 1 vault ([413,215,448,239] in f0867; [372,159,441,213] in f0987). KC-RDP stays at the server. A key-tooth nub is visible under the capsule inside CA1 in B-04.3_c.
findings.why: The RDP server's private key is transmitted to the issuing CA inside the certificate request. This is the core misrepresentation the film exists to prevent (F-03, F-04). A viewer learns that enrollment sends the private key to the CA.
findings.direction: Only the sealed capsule (public key and request info) may travel. The private key stays locked in the server's container throughout S4.

findings.evidence: When the capsule is consumed, the RDP private key does not leave with it. It moves to Issuing CA 1's signing press ([470,159,514,190] in f1035; [432,176,467,200] in f1077). The white hook-shaped key sits under the press head in frame b (about x475 y170), in frame c (about x445 y185) and in strip tiles 3-6, while the card is stamped.
findings.why: With the end-entity's private key at the CA press during issuance, the shot reads as the server's key taking part in the CA's signing. Only Issuing CA 1's own module key may drive the press (F-03; B-04.4 text).
findings.direction: Nothing but Issuing CA 1's sealed-module key may be associated with the press. No requester key may be present inside the CA.

findings.evidence: CERT-RDP and its CA1 copy return to rdp01 and lock beside KC-RDP ([554,343,625,403] at 9.55 m in f1110). KEY-RDP-PRIV is at [354,184,368,194] at 23.45 m, next to MODULE-CA1 at 23.49 m, still at the CA1 press (frame b, about x360 y185). In B-07.1_a the open rdp01 chassis shows its container without the key.
findings.why: The certificate is installed beside an emptied container, not 'beside the existing private key, which never moves'. The one-identity pairing (F-09) is broken and the key is held by the CA (F-03).
findings.direction: The card must lock beside the same, unmoved private key in KC-RDP, so that card and key visibly form one identity.

findings.evidence: In the desaturated setup-era flashback, KEY-RDP-PRIV is inside Issuing CA 1 at the press: [821,167,896,215] in f1246, [770,169,837,213] in f1249 and [359,148,391,170] in f1392. The white hook is visible beside the press head in each, and in strip tiles 1, 5 and 6.
findings.why: An end-entity private key that did not exist at setup appears inside the CA during the root ceremony. This implies that CAs hold subscriber private keys, and it muddles the subordinate-CA ceremony (AR-02, F-03).
findings.direction: Only Issuing CA 1's own key, in its sealed module, and its tagged CA request may appear in the flashback.

findings.evidence: From B-04.4 to the last frame, KEY-RDP-PRIV stays in the Issuing CA 1 vault: [723,178,730,183] in f1545, [259,173,269,180] in f2382, [200,353,207,360] in f2745, [870,181,881,188] in f2937, [424,326,429,330] in f3117 and [446,244,450,247] in f3267. In B-06.2 to B-06.4 it has no locator entry at all and cannot be located. It never returns to KC-RDP.
findings.why: The server cannot prove possession in the S6 handshake with a key held by Issuing CA 1. A trusted session is shown even though the server no longer owns its key, and the CA ends the film holding a subscriber's private key (F-10, F-03). Every beat from B-03.3 onward is therefore WRONG.
findings.direction: The RDP key must remain in KC-RDP inside rdp01 for the rest of the film. The B-06.1 key pulse must come from that container.

findings.evidence: None of the B-06.1 or B-09.1 frames or strip tiles shows the handshake proof (signature impression) travelling to the client and dissolving against the server card. Only the cards are seen arriving. B-09.1 shows no CRL scroll fetches either.
findings.why: 'A certificate alone proves nothing'. If proof of possession is not legible, presentation reads as 'sending the certificate authenticates the server'.
findings.direction: Make the signature impression visible and readable for long enough in B-06.1 and B-09.1, and make the B-09.1 per-link CRL fetches visible.

findings.evidence: The issuer links from the CA1 and CA2 crown certificates to the root are drawn plain white, not gold-to-cyan or gold. In B-07.3_c and B-07.4_a, Issuing CA 1 keeps its cyan interior instead of dimming to muted grey.
findings.why: The spec asks for a gold-to-cyan link (B-05.3), a gold link (B-08.3) and an ineligible CA in muted grey (B-07.3). Colour carries the issuer and eligibility meaning.
findings.direction: Use the root-gold to issuing-CA colour on trust links, and the ineligible grey token on CA1 in B-07.3.

findings.evidence: The 'Requester authenticated' tick is hidden behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' and '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' labels. In B-08.1, 'Name supplied in request - enrollment restricted' is drawn over 'Request meets template policy'.
findings.why: F-06 check 1 (authentication) is the check a viewer cannot read, and the F-07 restriction note is illegible.
findings.direction: Keep each of the four checks and the note unoccluded while they resolve.

findings.evidence: The caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' is on screen in B-06.5_c and B-06.6_a while the channel is still amber.
findings.why: The film claims trust before the connection visibly becomes trusted.
findings.direction: Bring the caption in only as or after the channel turns green.
